name: Neion Bio
summary: Neion Bio uses genetic engineering to turn chicken eggs into production systems for complex biologic medicines.
overview: Neion Bio is developing an egg-based biomanufacturing platform for biologics and biosimilars. It announced an oversubscribed $23 million Series A in June 2026, led by Caffeinated Capital, without a disclosed valuation.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Neion Bio announced an oversubscribed $23 million Series A; its valuation was not disclosed.

bull_case: If the Raptor platform produces difficult biologics at lower cost and with scalable, resilient manufacturing, Neion could address a meaningful bottleneck in drug supply.
bear_case: The path from a novel manufacturing platform to validated, regulated medicines is long. Technical scale-up, product quality and commercial adoption are material risks.
directory_notes: Clinical progress, scientific validation, and financing will be the key evidence points for future updates.

intelligence.description: Egg-based biologics manufacturing using genetic engineering and the Raptor platform.

metrics.note: Valuation was not announced with the Series A

company: Neion Bio uses genetic engineering to direct production of complex proteins into chicken eggs through its Raptor platform. The company is pursuing biologics, biosimilars, reagents, and animal-health applications.

In June 2026, Neion announced an oversubscribed $23 million Series A led by Caffeinated Capital. It said the financing followed emergence from stealth and a commercial co-development and supply agreement with a major pharmaceutical company.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Biologics manufacturing is expensive and capacity constrained. Neion's egg-based approach is a distinctive attempt to lower cost and shorten iteration cycles, but its value depends on scientific validation, regulatory progress and real commercial supply.

takeaways: Neion uses engineered chicken eggs as a production system for complex biologic proteins.
It announced a $23M Series A in June 2026 after a commercial co-development and supply agreement with a major pharmaceutical company.
Scientific validation, scale-up and regulatory progress will determine whether the platform can deliver its cost and speed promise.
No public valuation is asserted without a confirmed priced transaction.
